extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, OPLA staff, petitioners and practicing patent attorneys handling public-use/on-sale petitions and search documentation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for documenting search histories and for filing, handling, evaluating, hearing, and deciding petitions under 37 CFR 1.292 (public use/on-sale petitions) in USPTO prosecution, including examiner and OPLA procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete search history documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Required minimum documentation elements must be present when the history command is entered; missing elements must be documented by writing them on the printout of the search history or by supplying further portions of the search transcript which do include the missing elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the history display omits elements, document them manually on the printout or include additional transcript material; in some services the log off command supplies missing data elements (examples: STN and Questel-Orbit supply the database service name at log off; WEST does not print date and the date must be documented in writing). When results are reviewed, indicate reviewed results by circling them in BLACK INK.

rubrics_metrics.name: History Command should record search logic and file access
rubrics_metrics.description: The history command generally displays the search logic entered by the user and may display what file(s) were accessed; some services limit history displays to searches in the current file while others provide a complete record since sign on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the history command does not display files or full activity, capture file names and access via log off output or other available pages/prints. For structure/sequence searches, include printout of the structure/sequence used (e.g., STN structure printout using 'd L# que stat').

rubrics_metrics.name: Record the Name of Database Service
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the database service must be recorded as part of the search documentation; a file number alone is not adequate documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most services do not include the service name in the history command (WEST is an exception). Where the service does not display its name, supply it by including the log off command output or by writing it on the search record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Search Logic (query commands/structures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search Logic: record the search commands executed by the search software; for structure or sequence searches, the structure or sequence used must be printed out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the search logic is sufficiently detailed so the search can be understood and replicated; capture command strings and any structure/sequence prints (e.g., STN structure command guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Name of File Searched (not just file number)
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the file searched is required; some services display only a number and the name must be documented separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a service (e.g., Dialog) supplies only a file number on log off, write or otherwise record the file name since the number alone is inadequate for documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Date of Search
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of the search must be documented; some services (e.g., WEST, Dialog, Questel-Orbit) do not display the date as part of the history command and the date must therefore be supplied separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the date on the search report or include log off output that contains the date; ensure date is unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for other/publicly accessible databases (CD-ROM, specialized)
rubrics_metrics.description: For CD-ROM and other publicly accessible databases, record sufficient data to uniquely identify the material searched and sufficient information about the search query/request so the search can be updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the database location and form (e.g., 'CD-ROM'), version information, and sample citation format (examples provided: Entrez: Sequences, NCBI, Version ... (CD-ROM, TC 1600) Searched HIV and vaccine; date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify related earlier-filed applications in file wrapper or bib-data sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The file wrapper or the PALM bib-data sheet should identify earlier filed related applications (e.g., applications relied upon for benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is in the Image File Wrapper (IFW), print a bib-data sheet and the examiner should verify continuity and foreign priority information; write 'none' if no continuity/priority data exists and submit the initialed bib-data sheet for scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal contents of a petition under 37 CFR 1.292
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.292 must be submitted in writing, must specifically identify the application by application number or serial number and filing date, and should include a listing of all affidavits or declarations and exhibits relied on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must contain a sufficient description of the subject matter alleged to have been in 'public use' or 'on sale,' including necessary photographs, drawings, diagrams, exhibits, or flowcharts to enable the examiner to compare the claimed subject matter to the alleged public use/on-sale matter. The petition and accompanying papers must either (A) reflect that a copy has been served upon the applicant or applicant's attorney/agent or (B) be filed in duplicate if service is not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required identifying information on the petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition should clearly identify the application and include, if known: (A) Name of Applicant(s); (B) Application number; (C) Confirmation number; (D) Filing date of application; (E) Title of invention; (F) Technology Center art unit number; (G) Name of examiner assigned; (H) Current status and location of application; (I) The word 'ATTENTION:' followed by the area of the Office to which the petition is directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition itself should be identified as a 'PETITION UNDER 37 CFR 1.292.' Exhibits/attachments should contain identifying information to prevent separation or loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements and duplicate filing practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners must serve the petition on the applicant in accordance with 37 CFR 1.248 or file a duplicate with the Office when service is not possible; duplicate copies should be submitted only after diligent effort to serve has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an appropriate 'Certificate of Service' when filing to demonstrate service. If service cannot be made and duplicates are filed, OPLA will attempt to get the duplicate to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.292 must be submitted prior to the earliest of the date the application was published or the mailing of a notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.311, whichever occurs first; otherwise the petition will be dismissed as untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit petitions as soon as possible after becoming aware of the application to ensure maximum consideration. A petition submitted but not provided to OPLA before issuance/abandonment may be entered but dismissed as moot; petitions filed after final rejection may be considered if application still pending and unpublished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special timing rules for reissue application petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition with regard to a reissue application should be filed within the 2-month period following announcement of the filing of the reissue application in the Official Gazette; later filing is possible but will be scrutinized and may require a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 and payment of 1.17(f) fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners may request waiver of the 2-month delay under 37 CFR 1.183 (with fee). Requests for extensions will be critically reviewed; make requests only when necessary and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how to file and mark 'REISSUE LITIGATION' petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition can be submitted by mail to the Commissioner for Patents and should be directed to the attention of the director of the Technology Center; petitions directed to reissue applications involved in litigation should be marked 'REISSUE LITIGATION' on the outside envelope and top right-hand portion of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings preferably in a bright color; hand-carrying 'REISSUE LITIGATION' petitions to the Customer Service Window may help ensure prompt receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPLA preliminary handling checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: OPLA staff will ascertain whether the formal requirements of 37 CFR 1.292 have been fulfilled, including timeliness (before publication/notice of allowance), whether the alleged use/sale occurred more than 1 year before effective filing date, whether affidavits/declarations/exhibits are present, whether duplicate copies or service exist, and whether required fee has been tendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPLA orders the application file and ascertains status so appropriate action may be taken; papers not physically entered in the file will still be publicly available with the file wrapper; OPLA may reproduce a short petition rather than delay referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s standard for prima facie showing
rubrics_metrics.description: A prima facie case is established if the examiner finds that the facts asserted in the affidavits or declarations, as supported by exhibits, if later proved true by testimony taken in the public use proceeding, would result in a statutory bar to the claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) alone or in combination with 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine this, the examiner must identify exactly what was in public use or on sale, whether it was in use/on sale in this country more than one year before the effective filing date, and whether the pending claims 'read' on or are obvious over the alleged matter. Compare all pending claims with the alleged matter, not just claims identified by petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for petitions alleging obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: When the petition alleges only that the claims are obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale, the petition should include prior art or other information on which it relies and explain how the prior art or other information in combination with the asserted subject matter renders the claims obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner is not expected to perform a prior art search when evaluating the petition; however, if the examiner is aware of prior art that renders the claims obvious in combination with the alleged public use/on-sale matter, the examiner may determine a prima facie case has been made out even if the petition alleged only anticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner memorandum/report to OPLA after prima facie determination
rubrics_metrics.description: After making the determination, the examiner will forward a memorandum to the OPLA staff member stating findings and the decision as to whether a prima facie case has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The findings should include a summary of the alleged facts, a comparison of at least one claim with the device alleged to be in public use or on sale, and any other pertinent facts to aid OPLA in conducting the preliminary hearing. The report should be prepared in triplicate and addressed to the OPLA staff member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary hearing restrictions and format
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner concludes a prima facie case has been established, the Director may hold a preliminary hearing; no new evidence is to be introduced at this hearing, and the format of the hearing is established by OPLA staff; the examiner may attend only as an observer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ex parte situations, petitioner is not entitled to inspect the pending application; care must be taken to avoid discussing matters of the application not already known to petitioner. The hearing notice functions as an order to show cause why proceedings should not be instituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony rules in public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory bar can only be established by testimony taken in accordance with normal rules of evidence, including the right of cross-examination; affidavits or declarations and exhibits presented with the petition are not part of the testimony unless submitted as part of the petitioner's testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure is similar to taking testimony in an interference. Examiner sets a schedule for testimony and filing of records and briefs; a certified transcript of a deposition must be filed in the USPTO within one month after the date of deposition as provided by 37 CFR 41.157. All papers must be served per 37 CFR 1.248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard schedule for testimony, records and briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical schedule components: (A) petitioner testimony to close (approx. 60 days), (B) applicant objections to admissibility (approx. 20 days after A), (C) petitioner supplemental evidence to overcome objections (20 days after B), (D) time for applicant to request cross-examination (approx. 20 days after C), (E) time for cross-examination (approx. 30 days after D), (F) rebuttal testimony by applicant (approx. 20 days after E); record and exhibits and briefs filed in set intervals thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may agree on a different schedule provided the last brief is due no later than the date set forth and a copy of the new schedule is filed. No extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a); petitions to extend last-brief time must be filed under 37 CFR 1.136(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: In all public use proceedings, testimony will be limited to the issues of public use or on sale; no testimony will be received on whether the claimed subject matter would have been obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obviousness questions may be addressed differently (e.g., via prior art and legal analysis) but are not proper topics for testimony in the public use proceeding itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision requirements and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's final decision should be analogous to a Board (Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences) decision in an interference: analyze the testimony and state conclusions; the examiner is not bound by the prior finding that a prima facie case has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner concludes a public use or sale bar exists, enter a rejection predicated on the evidence and findings from the public use proceeding. Even if no rejection is made, the examiner's written action should indicate that the evidence of 35 U.S.C. 102(b) activity has been considered. The use of reasons for allowance under 37 CFR 1.104(e) may be appropriate. In ex parte cases where petitioner lacks access to the file, no copy of the examiner's action is mailed to the petitioner.
